We need propose a 3-step retrosynthesis for target SMILES: Cc1ccc(NS(=O)(=O)c2ccc(/C=C/C(=O)Nc3ccccc3N)cc2)cc1

We have guidance: steps forward: 1) amide formation (carboxylic acid + amine). 2) Doebner modification (aldehyde + malonic acid -> α,β-unsaturated acid). 3) sulfonamide formation (amine + sulfonyl chloride). So retrosynthetic steps reverse: target -> break amide to give acid and amine; then break α,β-unsaturated acid to aldehyde + malonic acid? Actually Doebner modification forward: aromatic aldehyde + malonic acid -> α,β-unsaturated carboxylic acid (with decarboxylation). So reverse: α,β-unsaturated acid -> aromatic aldehyde + malonic acid (or maybe malonic acid decarboxylates to give aldehyde? Wait forward: aldehyde + malonic acid -> α,β-unsaturated acid (with decarboxylation). So reverse: α,β-unsaturated acid -> aldehyde + malonic acid (or malonic acid derivative). So we can propose that the unsaturated side chain (C=C-C(=O)N...) originates from an aldehyde (maybe p-tolyl aldehyde?) Actually the side chain is /C=C/C(=O)N... The unsaturated acid after amide formation is C=C-C(=O)N... The amide formation step is after Doebner, so the unsaturated acid is C=C-C(=O) (carboxylic acid). Then amide formation attaches an aniline (Nc3ccccc3N). So reverse: break amide to give unsaturated acid and aniline (c3ccccc3N). Then break unsaturated acid to give aldehyde (maybe p-tolyl aldehyde?) and malonic acid? The unsaturated acid is attached to aromatic ring via /C=C/. The aromatic ring is c2ccc(... )cc2 attached to sulfonyl group. The unsaturated chain is attached to that aromatic ring at para position? The SMILES: ...c2ccc(/C=C/C(=O)Nc3ccccc3N)cc2. So the aromatic ring (c2) has a para substituent of the unsaturated amide chain. So the aldehyde precursor would be the same aromatic ring with an aldehyde at that position: c2ccc(CHO)cc2. So step 2: aromatic aldehyde (p-tolyl? Actually the ring has no substituents besides the sulfonyl group and the side chain). So the aldehyde is p-? The ring also has sulfonyl attached at para? The sulfonyl attaches to the first phenyl (c1) via NS(=O)(=O) linking to second phenyl (c2). So the second phenyl has the unsaturated chain at para relative to sulfonyl? Anyway.

Step 3: sulfonamide formation: the sulfonyl chloride reacts with an amine (the first phenyl has an amine attached to sulfonyl). So reverse: break sulfonamide to give sulfonyl chloride (or sulfonyl group attached to aromatic ring) and aniline (the first phenyl with NH2). So we need to propose precursors: 1) aromatic amine (p-toluidine?) Actually the first phenyl is Cc1ccc(N... )cc1 with a methyl at position 1 (para? The SMILES: Cc1ccc(NS(=O)(=O)c2... )cc1. So it's a tolyl (methyl) phenyl with sulfonamide attached. So the amine precursor is p-toluidine (4-methylaniline). The sulfonyl chloride precursor is p-tolyl sulfonyl chloride? Actually the sulfonyl group attached to second phenyl (c2). The sulfonyl chloride would be something like p-tolylsulfonyl chloride? Wait the sulfonyl group is attached to the first phenyl via N-SO2- linking to second phenyl. So the sulfonyl chloride precursor would be something like p-tolylsulfonyl chloride (ClSO2-Ph-? Actually sulfonyl chloride attached to second phenyl: the sulfonyl group is attached to the second phenyl via S(=O)(=O)c2... So the sulfonyl chloride would be p-tolylsulfonyl chloride (ClSO2-Ph-). Then reacting with p-toluidine gives sulfonamide linking the two phenyls.

Thus retrosynthesis:

Target -> (1) break amide: gives unsaturated acid (aryl-CH=CH-COOH) attached to second phenyl, and aniline (c3ccccc3N). The unsaturated acid is: Cc1ccc(NS(=O)(=O)c2ccc(/C=C/COOH)cc2)cc1? Actually after breaking amide, we have carboxylic acid attached to the unsaturated chain: /C=C/COOH attached to second phenyl. So precursor A: aromatic aldehyde (c2ccc(CHO)cc2) with sulfonyl attached to first phenyl? Wait the sulfonyl remains attached to first phenyl. So we have intermediate B: Cc1ccc(NS(=O)(=O)c2ccc(/C=C/COOH)cc2)cc1 (the unsaturated acid). Then step 2: break unsaturated acid to aldehyde + malonic acid. So precursor C: aromatic aldehyde (c2ccc(CHO)cc2) with sulfonyl attached to first phenyl. And malonic acid (HOOC-CH2-COOH). Step 3: break sulfonamide to give p-toluidine (4-methylaniline) and p-tolylsulfonyl chloride (ClSO2-Ph-CH3). The sulfonyl chloride attaches to second phenyl? Actually the sulfonyl chloride is attached to the second phenyl (the one bearing the aldehyde). So the sulfonyl chloride is p-tolylsulfonyl chloride (CH3-Ph-SO2Cl). The amine is p-toluidine (CH3-Ph-NH2). Reaction forms sulfonamide linking the two phenyls.

Thus final three steps:

Step1 (retro amide): target -> unsaturated acid + aniline (aniline is 4-aminophenyl? Actually Nc3ccccc3N is an aniline with an extra NH? The SMILES Nc3ccccc3N indicates an aniline with an extra NH attached? Actually it's an aniline where the amide nitrogen is attached to a phenyl that also has an NH (aniline). So the amine is 4-aminophenyl? The SMILES: Nc3ccccc3N means an aniline with an amino group at position 1? Actually it's a phenyl with two amino substituents: one at position 1 (attached to amide) and another at position? The SMILES "Nc3ccccc3N" is an aniline with an extra NH at the other end? It is a phenyl with two NH groups at positions 1 and maybe 4? But it's symmetrical? Anyway we can treat as 1,4-diaminobenzene? Actually "Nc3ccccc3N" is an aniline where the nitrogen attached to carbonyl is attached to the aromatic carbon, and there is another NH attached to the same aromatic carbon? Wait the SMILES: N c3 c c c c c3 N. That is an aniline where the aromatic carbon has an NH attached (the amide) and also the aromatic ring has an NH at the other end (para). So it's p-phenylenediamine (1,4-diaminobenzene). So the amine precursor is p-phenylenediamine.

Thus step1: target -> unsaturated acid (aryl-CH=CH-COOH) attached to second phenyl, plus p-phenylenediamine.

Step2: unsaturated acid -> aromatic aldehyde (aryl-CHO) + malonic acid.

Step3: sulfonamide formation reverse: the sulfonyl chloride (p-tolylsulfonyl chloride) + p-toluidine (or p-phenylenediamine?) Wait the sulfonamide is between the first phenyl (with methyl) and the second phenyl (with sulfonyl). The sulfonyl chloride would be p-tolylsulfonyl chloride (CH3-Ph-SO2Cl). The amine would be p-toluidine (CH3-Ph-NH2). But the amine we have from step1 is p-phenylenediamine, which has two NH groups; one used for amide, the other for sulfonamide? Actually the amide uses the NH attached to the phenyl (the one that is part of p-phenylenediamine). The other NH could be used for sulfonamide formation with sulfonyl chloride. So the amine precursor is p-phenylenediamine, which can react both ways: one NH forms amide with the unsaturated acid, the other NH forms sulfonamide with sulfonyl chloride. So step3: p-phenylenediamine + p-tolylsulfonyl chloride -> the sulfonamide linking the two phenyls (the first phenyl is p-tolyl). Wait the first phenyl is methyl-substituted (C). So the sulfonyl chloride is attached to the second phenyl (which is also methyl-substituted? Actually the second phenyl is not methyl-substituted; the first phenyl has methyl. The sulfonyl chloride is derived from the second phenyl? The sulfonyl chloride is attached to the second phenyl (c2). That phenyl is unsubstituted except the side chain. So the sulfonyl chloride would be phenylsulfonyl chloride (ClSO2-Ph). But the first phenyl has methyl. So the sulfonyl chloride is phenylsulfonyl chloride (no methyl). The amine is p-toluidine (methyl phenyl amine). That matches: the sulfonyl chloride attaches to the second phenyl (no methyl) and the amine is p-toluidine (methyl phenyl). So step3: p-toluidine + phenylsulfonyl chloride -> sulfonamide linking them.

Thus final route:

Target (M0)

Retro step1 (amide cleavage): M0 -> M1 (aryl-CH=CH-COOH attached to phenyl-sulfonyl) + p-phenylenediamine (or maybe aniline with extra NH). But we need three steps total, so we can combine sulfonamide formation as step3, and amide formation as step1, Doebner as step2.

Thus we need to provide JSON with hierarchy: root molecule target, children: reaction1 (amide formation) leading to precursors: M1 (unsaturated acid) and aniline (p-phenylenediamine). Then M1 children: reaction2 (Doebner) leading to aldehyde (aryl-CHO) and malonic acid. Then aldehyde children: reaction3 (sulfonamide) leading to p-toluidine and phenylsulfonyl chloride.

We need template IDs for each reaction. We have template 401931 for amide formation (looks like amide formation from acid and amine). Use that as template_id for step1.

For Doebner modification, need a template that breaks C=C double bond and forms aldehyde and carboxylic acid? Actually forward Doebner forms unsaturated acid from aldehyde + malonic acid. Reverse: unsaturated acid -> aldehyde + malonic acid. We need a template that matches that transformation. Search for functional_groups_broken: ["C-C double bonds"] and formed: ["aldehydes", "carboxylic acid"] but we got error because carboxylic acid not valid; need "aliphatic carboxylic acid" or "aromatic carboxylic acid". The product after reverse is aldehyde (aryl aldehyde) and malonic acid (aliphatic carboxylic acid). So functional_groups_formed: ["aldehydes", "aliphatic carboxylic acid"]. Let's search.
